<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Prompt for WebVoyager</h2>

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The System Prompt for WebVoyager is shown in Figure <a href="#A3.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ Appendix C Action Space ‣ WebVoyager : Building an End-to-End Web Agent with Large Multimodal Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>. The Prompt’s guidelines hold potential for optimization and should be generalist rather than website-specific in design. Incorporating specific issues from websites into the system prompt may compromise the agent’s universality.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Prompt for Auto Evaluation</h2>

<div id="A2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A5.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ Appendix E Additional Related Work ‣ WebVoyager : Building an End-to-End Web Agent with Large Multimodal Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> demonstrates using GPT-4V as an evaluator for web tasks, involving web task instruction, screenshots in the trajectory, and WebVoyager responses. We require GPT-4V to mark success or not success. The temperature is set to 0 to reduce randomness during evaluation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Action Space</h2>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We detail the interaction actions that WebVoyager employs to navigate and operate within web environments. These actions are fundamental to how the agent interacts with web pages, retrieves information, and performs specific tasks as part of its operational protocol. The actions range from basic web navigation to more complex operations, tailored to efficiently gather data and respond to queries. Each action is designed with a specific format for easy identification and execution.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="A3.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A3.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A3.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Click. This action involves clicking on an element within a webpage, typically a link or a button.
If clicking a link results in the download of a PDF file, we automatically parse its content using the OpenAI Assistant API<span id="footnote8" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">8</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">8</sup>
                  <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">8</span>
                  
                  
                  
                https://platform.openai.com/docs/assistants/overview</span></span></span> and incorporate it into the Observation. Action Format: <span id="A3.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Click [Numerical_Label]</span>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A3.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A3.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Input. This is a composite action that involves selecting a text box, deleting any existing content within it, and then inputting new content.
To minimize interaction frequency, an automatic ENTER key press follows the input completion. Action Format: <span id="A3.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Type [Numerical_Label]; [Content]</span>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A3.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A3.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Scroll. Scrolling is a common operation for browsing webpages, usually involving the vertical movement of the entire page.
However, there are instances where only a specific section within the webpage is scrollable. In such cases, we expect the Agent to select an element within the scrollable area and navigate to that particular region for scrolling. Action Format: <span id="A3.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Scroll [Numerical_Label or WINDOW]; [up or down]</span>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A3.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A3.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Wait. Action execution requires time, and this action is often used to wait for web pages to load.
Action Format: <span id="A3.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Wait</span>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A3.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A3.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Back. This action is used to return to the previous page.
We consider the forward action unnecessary because it can be achieved by repeating previous actions. Action Format: <span id="A3.I1.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">GoBack</span>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A3.I1.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A3.I1.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.I1.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Jump to Search Engine. There are often situations where agents get stuck at a certain website, without finding an answer. This action enables the agent to jump to a search engine and start anew.
In this work, we just adopt Google Search. Action Format: <span id="A3.I1.i6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Google</span>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A3.I1.i7" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A3.I1.i7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.I1.i7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Answer. Once all questions in the task are resolved, this action concludes the iteration and provides an answer in line with the task requirements.
Action Format: <span id="A3.I1.i7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">ANSWER; [Content]</span>.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<figure id="A3.F7" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2401.13919v4/prompt.svg" id="A3.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:462/354;" width="462" height="354"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 7: </span>System Prompt for WebVoyager. We instruct agents to perform web navigation, along with specific browsing actions and action formats. To enhance efficiency and accuracy, we can incorporate additional general into the prompts. These guidelines should be generic and not about a specific website to ensure generalizability.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Additional Trajectories</h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In Figure <a href="#S4.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 4.3 Annotation Process ‣ 4 Benchmark for WebVoyager ‣ WebVoyager : Building an End-to-End Web Agent with Large Multimodal Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, we demonstrate how WebVoyager automatically navigates the Apple website and accomplishes the task.
In this section, we exhibit the trajectories for the remaining websites that complete web tasks successfully. We provide a screenshot for each step, accompanied by the action generated by WebVoyager. The specific navigation trajectories for each website are illustrated in Figures <a href="#A6.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ Appendix F Error Cases ‣ WebVoyager : Building an End-to-End Web Agent with Large Multimodal Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> to <a href="#A6.F22" title="Figure 22 ‣ Appendix F Error Cases ‣ WebVoyager : Building an End-to-End Web Agent with Large Multimodal Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">22</span></a>. In addition, we also explore the performance of WebVoyager on websites in other languages, and we provide two example trajectories in Chinese and Spanish in Figure <a href="#A6.F23" title="Figure 23 ‣ Appendix F Error Cases ‣ WebVoyager : Building an End-to-End Web Agent with Large Multimodal Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">23</span></a> and Figure <a href="#A6.F24" title="Figure 24 ‣ Appendix F Error Cases ‣ WebVoyager : Building an End-to-End Web Agent with Large Multimodal Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">24</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Additional Related Work</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Vision-based Agents</span> Concurrent to our work, a few related works also studied vision-based autonomous agents. VisualWebArena <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Koh et al. (2024)</a></cite> extends WebArena with additional websites and tasks that focus on visual reasoning to facilitate research on vision-based web agents. SeeClick <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cheng et al. (2024)</a></cite> focused on finetuning an LMM to solely leverage screenshots as inputs to interact with websites. WebVLN <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al. (2023)</a></cite> introduced a web simulator that provides both HTML text and screenshots to finetune supervised vision-language models. GPT-4V Wonderland <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yan et al. (2023)</a></cite> and AppAgent <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib48" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al. (2023)</a></cite> instead focus on building agents that can operate smartphone apps using the GPT-4V as the backbone. These works further underscore the promising prospects in this field.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Large Multimodal Models</span>.
In recent years, significant strides have been made in unifying image and text representations within a single multimodal model through joint training with image and text <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2019</a>; <a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dosovitskiy et al., 2020</a>; <a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dai et al., 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Aghajanyan et al., 2022</a>)</cite>.
Large Multimodal Models (LMMs), following in the footsteps of Large Language Models <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Brown et al., 2020</a>; <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chowdhery et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, attain the capability of instruction following <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ouyang et al., 2022</a>)</cite> and exhibit robust multimodal comprehension. Represented by GPT-4V <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">OpenAI, 2023</a>)</cite> and Gemini <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Team et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, LMMs have demonstrated impressive performance on benchmarks <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Goyal et al., 2017</a>; <a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lu et al., 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zellers et al., 2019</a>; <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hessel et al., 2022</a>)</cite>, establishing a foundation for the construction of multimodal agents in subsequent research.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A5.F8" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2401.13919v4/prompt_auto.svg" id="A5.F8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:467/245;" width="467" height="245"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 8: </span>System Prompt for Auto Evaluation by GPT-4V.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Error Cases</h2>

<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we provide specific examples of the four types of errors mentioned in the Error Analysis section. Figure <a href="#A6.F25" title="Figure 25 ‣ Appendix F Error Cases ‣ WebVoyager : Building an End-to-End Web Agent with Large Multimodal Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">25</span></a> illustrates a snippet of WebVoyager navigating on Google Flights and a Visual Grounding Issue appears. The task is to retrieve one-way flight information for January 22nd; however, it selects December 22nd on the Calendar and fails to make the necessary corrections. Although it attempts to modify the date in step 6, it ultimately fails to do so. Figure <a href="#A6.F26" title="Figure 26 ‣ Appendix F Error Cases ‣ WebVoyager : Building an End-to-End Web Agent with Large Multimodal Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">26</span></a> illustrates a situation of WebVoyager navigating on Allrecipes, encountering the Navigation Stuck issue. The agent requires multiple downward scrolls to locate the correct ingredients. However, it experiences confusion during the process, and it is uncertain whether to scroll up or down. Figure <a href="#A6.F27" title="Figure 27 ‣ Appendix F Error Cases ‣ WebVoyager : Building an End-to-End Web Agent with Large Multimodal Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">27</span></a> depicts the Hallucination issue encountered by WebVoyager on the Coursera website. In the task, we query the number of quizzes in the "Artificial Intelligence for Healthcare" course. However, the agent only identifies the quiz in module 1 of the course, which is not the optimal answer and does not fulfill the task requirements. Figure <a href="#A6.F28" title="Figure 28 ‣ Appendix F Error Cases ‣ WebVoyager : Building an End-to-End Web Agent with Large Multimodal Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">28</span></a> illustrates the issue of Prompt Misalignment encountered while browsing BBC News. WebVoyager fails to fulfill all the task requirements. Instead of completing the navigation, it provides partial answers and tells me how to find complete answers, which is not end-to-end.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A6.F9" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2401.13919v4/allrecipes_4.png" id="A6.F9.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/273;" width="476" height="273" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 9: </span>Screenshots of a complete trajectory of browsing Allrecipes. </figure>
<figure id="A6.F10" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2401.13919v4/Amazon_0.png" id="A6.F10.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/148;" width="476" height="148" alt="Refer to caption">

</figure>

Given the task: “Identify a course on Coursera related to ’Artificial Intelligence for Healthcare’ and note the course duration along with the number of quizzes in Assessments.” The agent provides the answer: “Module 1 includes 3 quizzes in the Assessments.” However, we also require other Modules and agent fails to provide the results.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A6.F28" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2401.13919v4/error_BBC_11.png" id="A6.F28.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/134;" width="476" height="134" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 28: </span>An error case for BBC News. Given the task: “Find out how many teams are in the Scottish Premiership of the Football Tournament and when did the Hibernian team’s most recent match start?” The agent provides the answer: “There are 12 teams in the Scottish Premiership. To find out the exact start time of Hibernian’s most recent match, further interaction with the website would be required.” The Agent knows that the task is not yet complete, but it ends its navigation early, even though it can find the Hibernian team’s most recent match.</figcaption>
</figure>

    </ul>
    <p><strong>Tip:</strong> You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.</p>
    <p>Our team has already identified <a class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/arXiv/html_feedback/issues"
        target="_blank">the following issues</a>. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we
      may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability
      should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
      all.</p>
    <p>Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a <a
        class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/wiki/Porting-LaTeX-packages-for-LaTeXML"
        target="_blank">list of packages that need conversion</a>, and welcome <a class="ltx_ref"
        href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/issues" target="_blank">developer contributions</a>.</p>
  </div>
